errors.discriminating_probe: Ask why the function is continuous on the closed interval: an answer that the theorem's name is enough is consistent with BC-MIS-05002, an answer that the conclusion may be used regardless is consistent with BC-MIS-99009, and a correct spoken answer with the sentence missing only on paper is consistent with the transfer and timing causes.
errors.name: Continuity not drawn from the given differentiability
non_conceptual_causes: the continuity sentence is written on scratch work and never transferred to the response
the stem's phrase differentiable on the closed interval is skimmed and read as already continuous
the part is reached late and the hypothesis sentence is the first thing cut
errors.observed_behavior: The response asserts that the function is continuous without saying that differentiability supplies it, or omits continuity altogether.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point tied to the hypothesis is lost; the 2025 guideline refused a bare statement that the function is continuous.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the quotient written symbolically before any numbers are substituted: averaging the two endpoint values is consistent with BC-MIS-05003, an integral divided by the interval length is consistent with BC-MIS-99006, and a correct symbolic form carrying a wrong number is consistent with the column and keying causes.
errors.name: Average rate of change formed incorrectly
non_conceptual_causes: the two endpoint values are read from the wrong table columns
the subtraction is keyed into the calculator in the reversed order
the denominator is taken as one endpoint rather than the difference of the endpoints
errors.observed_behavior: The response averages the two endpoint values, reverses the order of subtraction, or divides by the wrong difference.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point for the average rate of change is lost and any solved value built on it is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to state the conclusion in one sentence: naming the theorem but not the claim is consistent with BC-MIS-05002, asserting the claim with no theorem is consistent with BC-MIS-01016, and producing both fluently on request is consistent with the transfer and misreading causes.
errors.name: Existence asserted with no affirmative answer or no theorem
non_conceptual_causes: the affirmative sentence is spoken while working and never written
the theorem name is left on scratch work with the arithmetic
the stem is read as a computation because the previous part asked for one
errors.observed_behavior: The response computes the needed arithmetic but never says yes and never names a theorem.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; the guideline requires an affirmative answer in some form.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the reported input lies strictly between the endpoints: treating the open interval as an optional detail is consistent with BC-MIS-99009, treating any solution of the equation as the theorem's output is consistent with BC-MIS-01016, and discarding the stray root once asked is consistent with the root selection and misreading causes.
errors.name: Solved value reported outside the open interval
non_conceptual_causes: the second root of a quadratic is kept without testing it against the interval
the interval endpoints are misread from the stem
the value is reported straight from the calculator solver with no domain check
errors.observed_behavior: The response solves the derivative equation and reports a solution that is an endpoint or lies outside the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost because the theorem places the point strictly inside the interval.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which theorem concerns values of the function and which concerns values of the derivative: one theorem offered for both kinds of claim is consistent with BC-MIS-05005, a name supplied as the whole justification is consistent with BC-MIS-05002, and a correct distinction with the wrong name on paper is consistent with the copying and misreading causes.
errors.name: Intermediate Value Theorem cited for a claim about the derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the theorem is chosen because it is the one most recently practised
the stem's symbol for the derivative value is read as a function value
the theorem name is copied from a neighbouring part of the same question
errors.observed_behavior: The response justifies the existence of an input with a given derivative value by appealing to the Intermediate Value Theorem.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost outright; the 2023 guideline names this as disqualifying.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what happens on the same interval for a function with a jump in the middle: an answer that the extrema still exist is consistent with BC-MIS-05006, an answer that the hypotheses need not be established is consistent with BC-MIS-99009, and spotting the jump at once is consistent with the misreading and transfer causes.
errors.name: Extreme Value Theorem invoked without continuity on the closed interval
non_conceptual_causes: the break in the piecewise definition is not noticed in the stem
the interval is copied as closed where the stem wrote it open
the hypothesis is checked on the graph and never written down
errors.observed_behavior: The response claims that a maximum and a minimum are attained for a function with a break inside the interval, or on an open interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The hypothesis point is lost and the conclusion is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the theorem tells you and what it does not: claiming it names the input is consistent with BC-MIS-01016, offering the name in place of the argument is consistent with BC-MIS-05002, and separating existence from location on request is consistent with the misreading and carry-over causes.
errors.name: Existence theorem used to locate the extremum
non_conceptual_causes: the question's word where is read as whether
the extremum located in an earlier part is carried into this one
the theorem is recalled from a worked example that also located the extremum
errors.observed_behavior: The response treats the Extreme Value Theorem as though it named the input at which the extremum occurs.
errors.scoring_consequence: The response answers a different question and the location it reports is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what equation produced the listed inputs: an answer that any listed input is automatically an extremum is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, an answer that the list is itself the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, and reciting the equation immediately is consistent with the calculator and transfer causes.
errors.name: Zeros of the derivative listed without stating the derivative condition
non_conceptual_causes: the equation is solved on the calculator and only the roots are copied
the setup line is written on scratch work and not transferred
the part is written last and only the answer line is filled
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes down the inputs at which the derivative vanishes but never presents the equation setting the derivative equal to zero.
errors.scoring_consequence: The first point of the candidates test is lost; the 2023 guideline states that listing the zeros is not sufficient.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the function has a value at the disputed input: keeping it as a critical point regardless is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, treating the domain gap as not interrupting the behaviour is consistent with BC-MIS-05012, and dropping it once the domain is stated is consistent with the cancellation and calculator causes.
errors.name: Solutions outside the domain retained as critical points
non_conceptual_causes: a factor is cancelled from the derivative although it also vanishes in the denominator
the domain of the original function is never written down
the root comes from a calculator zero with no check that the function has a value there
errors.observed_behavior: The response keeps an input at which the derivative expression vanishes although the function itself is undefined there.
errors.scoring_consequence: The candidate list is wrong and the comparison that follows cannot be correct.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to mark every input where the derivative graph breaks: an answer that only zeros count is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, an answer that the derivative exists wherever the function does is consistent with BC-MIS-05009, and marking the corner correctly on request is consistent with the simplification and scale causes.
errors.name: Inputs where the derivative fails to exist omitted from the critical points
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative is read from a simplified formula that hides the corner
the sharp point on the figure reads as a smooth turn at the plotted scale
only the roots the solver returned are listed
errors.observed_behavior: The response finds only the zeros of the derivative and skips corners, cusps, and vertical tangents.
errors.scoring_consequence: A candidate is missing, so the comparison may select the wrong extremum and the justification is incomplete.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether any other input could give a larger value: an answer that a local high point is the highest is consistent with BC-MIS-05007, an answer that the local test settles the global question is consistent with BC-MIS-05018, and completing the comparison on request is consistent with the endpoint and timing causes.
errors.name: Relative extremum reported as the absolute extremum
non_conceptual_causes: the endpoint values are never evaluated
the word absolute in the stem is skimmed
the comparison table is begun and abandoned when the part runs out of time
errors.observed_behavior: The response finds a local high or low point and reports it as the largest or smallest value on the interval without comparing the rest.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost because the argument is local where a global claim was asked for.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign of the derivative immediately on each side: an answer that every critical point is an extremum is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, a classification drawn from the size of the derivative is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, and reporting the same sign twice once asked is consistent with the test point and multiplicity causes.
errors.name: Critical point with no sign change declared an extremum
non_conceptual_causes: the sign of the derivative is tested on one side of the input only
the test point chosen on one side lies beyond the next critical point
a factor of even multiplicity is charted as a sign change
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a relative maximum or minimum at an input where the derivative is zero but keeps its sign on both sides.
errors.scoring_consequence: The single answer with reason point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the derivative at one input inside the disputed interval: reading the derivative's sign from the function's sign is consistent with BC-MIS-05010, reading it from the second derivative is consistent with BC-MIS-05019, and a corrected sign on recomputation is consistent with the substitution and test point causes.
errors.name: Sign of the derivative misread on an interval
non_conceptual_causes: a test value is substituted into the function rather than into the derivative
the sign of a negative factor is dropped while multiplying the factors in the chart
the test point falls outside the interval it was meant to represent
errors.observed_behavior: The response assigns the wrong sign to the derivative expression on one of the intervals of its sign chart.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported intervals are wrong, which also forfeits the reason point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to label the plotted curve and the function under discussion separately before answering: treating the drawn curve as the function is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, treating the derivative as fixing the function outright is consistent with BC-MIS-05025, and labelling both correctly on request is consistent with the axis label and transcription causes.
errors.name: Plotted derivative read as the function itself
non_conceptual_causes: the axis label on the figure is not read
the figure is carried over from a previous part where the function itself was plotted
the curve is labelled correctly on scratch work and the answer sentence names the wrong object
errors.observed_behavior: The response answers a question about the function by describing features of the curve shown, which is the derivative.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every part that rests on the plotted object is answered about the wrong function.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for a curve that is decreasing and concave up at once: an answer that no such curve exists is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, an answer that the second derivative behaves like the first is consistent with BC-MIS-05019, and drawing it correctly while the written answer still swaps the two is consistent with the referent and ordering causes.
errors.name: Increase of the derivative confused with positivity of the derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the word increasing in the stem is attached to the plotted curve rather than to the function
the sign chart is built from the plotted curve's values instead of its slopes
the two questions inside the part are answered in the reverse order
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports concavity where monotonicity was asked for, or reports increase of the function where the derivative graph is rising.
errors.scoring_consequence: The intervals reported belong to the other question and the reason point is unavailable.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the domain of the function before the sign chart is drawn: an answer that a gap does not interrupt an interval is consistent with BC-MIS-05012, an answer that the derivative's sign follows the function's sign is consistent with BC-MIS-05010, and adding the missing partition point once the domain is stated is consistent with the cancellation and window causes.
errors.name: Sign chart omits a point where the function is undefined
non_conceptual_causes: the denominator is cancelled before the partition points are collected
the domain is never written down before the chart is drawn
the asymptote lies outside the calculator window that was used
errors.observed_behavior: The response partitions the number line at the zeros of the derivative only and ignores a vertical asymptote or a domain gap.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interval spans a break, so the reported behaviour is claimed where the function does not exist.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to rewrite the sentence with every pronoun replaced by a name: restating the conclusion as the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, treating the presence of symbols as completing the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05022, and naming the object correctly at once is consistent with the carry-over and timing causes.
errors.name: Justification uses an unnamed referent
non_conceptual_causes: the pronoun is carried over from the stem's own wording
the sentence is written at speed at the end of the part
the object is named once in an earlier part and treated as still named
errors.observed_behavior: The reason says that the function or the graph changes sign, without naming which object is meant.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost; the 2025 guideline names an ambiguous referent as disqualifying.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the function has a value at the input between the two stretches: merging them anyway is consistent with BC-MIS-05012, arguing from the function's own sign is consistent with BC-MIS-05010, and separating them on request is consistent with the transcription and window causes.
errors.name: Interval of increase reported across a gap in the domain
non_conceptual_causes: the two intervals are merged when the answer is copied from the sign chart
the undefined input lies outside the calculator window that was used
the union symbol is dropped in transcription
errors.observed_behavior: The response merges two intervals of increase into one although the function is undefined between them.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interval reported is wrong and the reason point falls with it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where a relative extremum is allowed to occur: an answer that any critical point qualifies is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, an answer that the candidate list is the critical points only is consistent with BC-MIS-05016, and naming the rule correctly while the written work still samples is consistent with the table and solving causes.
errors.name: Candidate extrema sought away from the critical points
non_conceptual_causes: inputs are sampled from a table supplied for a different part
the interval is scanned by substitution because the derivative looks hard to solve
the word relative in the stem is read as absolute, so endpoints are tested as well
errors.observed_behavior: The response tests inputs that are neither critical points nor endpoints when hunting for a relative extremum.
errors.scoring_consequence: Time is spent on inputs that cannot be extrema, and in a candidates argument extra inputs cost the justification point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to sketch the curve implied by their own sign statement: classifying from the derivative's value rather than its change is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, expecting the second derivative test to settle it is consistent with BC-MIS-05023, and a sketch that contradicts the written answer is consistent with the reading direction and transposition causes.
errors.name: Direction of the sign change reversed in the classification
non_conceptual_causes: the sign chart is read right to left
the plus and minus labels are transposed when the chart is copied
the classification is carried over from a second derivative test done in an earlier part
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a relative maximum where the derivative changes from negative to positive, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer with reason point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign of the derivative on each side, not its size: classifying by magnitude is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, treating every critical point as an extremum is consistent with BC-MIS-05008, and giving the signs correctly once asked is consistent with the calculator table and skipped chart causes.
errors.name: Classification taken from the value of the derivative rather than its change
non_conceptual_causes: the derivative values at the two test points are compared in size rather than in sign
the test points are read from a calculator table showing magnitudes only
the sign chart is skipped because the derivative looks monotone
errors.observed_behavior: The response classifies the critical point by whether the derivative is large or small nearby instead of by its sign change.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason does not express a sign change, so the point is lost even when the classification is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to state whether the derivative changes sign, in those words: a reason drawn from the derivative's values is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, a reason that restates the conclusion is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, and the correct phrase supplied at once is consistent with the copying and timing causes.
errors.name: Positive before and after offered in place of no sign change
non_conceptual_causes: the phrase is copied from a worked example
the conclusion sentence is written before the chart is finished
the chart is correct and the sentence paraphrases it loosely at the end of the part
errors.observed_behavior: The response justifies a classification of neither by saying the derivative is positive before and after the input.
errors.scoring_consequence: The point is lost; the 2023 guideline names this phrasing as insufficient while accepting a declaration that the derivative does not change sign.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to underline the noun the question asks for: treating location and value as the same answer is consistent with BC-MIS-05015, reporting whichever candidate was computed last is consistent with BC-MIS-05017, and correcting the answer immediately is consistent with the unlabelled table and transfer causes.
errors.name: Location reported where the value was asked for
non_conceptual_causes: the question's noun is skimmed and the other quantity is reported
the answer is copied from a candidate table whose columns are unlabelled
both quantities are computed and the wrong one is transferred to the answer line
errors.observed_behavior: The response names the input at which the extremum occurs when the question asked for the extreme value, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost; the 2023 guideline awarded it only for the minimum value, not for the input.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the listed inputs lie inside the stated interval: an answer that the critical points are the whole candidate list is consistent with BC-MIS-05016, an answer that the domain is all inputs is consistent with BC-MIS-05028, and striking the outside root on request is consistent with the misreading and solver causes.
errors.name: Critical points outside the interval included as candidates
non_conceptual_causes: the interval in the stem is misread
the critical points are carried over from an earlier part with a wider interval
the solver returns every root and every root is tabulated
errors.observed_behavior: The response carries a critical point that lies outside the closed interval into the candidate comparison.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost because inputs other than the candidates appear in the argument.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the function value at each end of the interval: an answer that only critical points are candidates is consistent with BC-MIS-05016, an answer that a local test settles the global question is consistent with BC-MIS-05018, and computing the endpoints readily is consistent with the timing and misreading causes.
errors.name: One or both endpoints omitted from the candidate comparison
non_conceptual_causes: the candidate table is begun with the interior points and the part ends before the ends are reached
the interval is read as open
the endpoint value needs a further integral that is left uncomputed
errors.observed_behavior: The response compares values only at the interior critical points and never evaluates at the ends of the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost; the 2023 guideline states that a response not considering both endpoints does not earn it.

errors.discriminating_probe: Recompute one disputed entry and compare with the table: a candidate list that was never questioned is consistent with BC-MIS-05016, reporting the last entry computed is consistent with BC-MIS-05017, and a corrected entry with the method intact is consistent with the sign and row causes.
errors.name: Function evaluated incorrectly at a candidate
non_conceptual_causes: a sign is dropped while substituting a negative input
the area of one region under the graph is counted without its sign
the accumulated value is taken from the wrong row of the table
errors.observed_behavior: One entry of the candidate table is wrong, whether by substitution or by an area computation.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification point is lost outright; the 2023 guideline withholds it for any evaluation error at a candidate.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which of the tabulated values is smallest: reporting whichever was computed last is consistent with BC-MIS-05017, reporting the input instead of the value is consistent with BC-MIS-05015, and picking correctly from the table on request is consistent with the ordering and magnitude causes.
errors.name: Extremum selected in the wrong direction
non_conceptual_causes: the largest entry is reported because the table was built in that order
the words maximum and minimum are transposed in the answer sentence
negative candidate values are compared by magnitude
errors.observed_behavior: The response compares the candidate values correctly but reports the largest where the smallest was asked for.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer point is lost although the table is right.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the second derivative at one input inside the disputed interval: treating the second derivative as behaving like the first is consistent with BC-MIS-05019, treating concavity and monotonicity as one property is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, and a corrected sign on recomputation is consistent with the substitution and differentiation causes.
errors.name: Sign of the second derivative misread
non_conceptual_causes: a test value is substituted into the first derivative instead of the second
a sign is dropped while differentiating the second time
the test point lies outside the interval it labels
errors.observed_behavior: The response assigns the wrong sign to the second derivative on one interval of its sign chart.
errors.scoring_consequence: The concavity intervals are wrong and the reason point is unavailable.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the plotted curve is rising or falling on the disputed stretch: conflating concavity with monotonicity is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, taking the plotted curve to be the function is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, and answering rising correctly while the written work used positive is consistent with the carry-over and wording causes.
errors.name: Concavity read from the sign of the plotted derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the chart is built from where the plotted curve lies above the axis because that is what an earlier part needed
the figure's axis label is not read
the words rising and positive are used interchangeably in the answer sentence
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports concave up where the plotted derivative is above the axis rather than where it is rising.
errors.scoring_consequence: The intervals reported are those of increase, so both the interval point and the reason point are lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the function has a value at the disputed input: treating every zero of the second derivative as an inflection point is consistent with BC-MIS-05021, treating a domain gap as not interrupting behaviour is consistent with BC-MIS-05012, and discarding the input once the domain is stated is consistent with the cancellation and solver causes.
errors.name: Second derivative zeros taken outside the domain of the function
non_conceptual_causes: the domain of the function is never written down
a common factor is cancelled before the zeros are collected
the root comes from a solver with no check that the function has a value there
errors.observed_behavior: The response lists a candidate point of inflection at an input where the function is not defined.
errors.scoring_consequence: The declared list contains an extra input, which costs the answer point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the second derivative does on each side of the disputed input: an answer that a zero suffices is consistent with BC-MIS-05021, an answer drawn from monotonicity instead is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, and reporting the sign change correctly on request is consistent with the listing and transfer causes.
errors.name: Point of inflection declared with no sign change checked
non_conceptual_causes: every zero of the plotted curve is listed because the part asks for a list
the sign of the second derivative is tested on one side only
the check is made on the figure and the written sentence reports the zeros alone
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports every zero of the second derivative, or every zero of the plotted curve, as a point of inflection.
errors.scoring_consequence: An extra input in the list costs the answer point outright.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to sketch the second derivative near that input: keeping the touching zero anyway is consistent with BC-MIS-05021, arguing from the derivative's value rather than its change is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, and a sketch showing the return to the same sign is consistent with the multiplicity and scale causes.
errors.name: Touching zero retained as a point of inflection
non_conceptual_causes: the repeated factor is charted as a single root
the curve's tangency to the axis reads as a crossing at the plotted scale
the sign is tested at points too far from the input to see the return
errors.observed_behavior: The response keeps an input where the second derivative reaches zero and returns to the same sign.
errors.scoring_consequence: The list has an extra entry, so the answer point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which plotted feature makes the second derivative change sign there: restating the conclusion as the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05013, treating the symbols as completing the reason is consistent with BC-MIS-05022, and naming the feature at once is consistent with the template and timing causes.
errors.name: Inflection reason restated in second derivative symbols
non_conceptual_causes: the symbolic sentence is copied from a memorised template
the plotted object is named in an earlier part and treated as still named
the justification is written at the end of the part in the shortest form to hand
errors.observed_behavior: The reason says that the second derivative changes sign there, without tying the claim to the plotted object the question supplied.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reason point is lost while the answer point stands; the 2025 guideline names this split directly.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the first derivative at that input: an answer that the second derivative test always decides is consistent with BC-MIS-05023, an answer that the two tests are interchangeable is consistent with BC-MIS-05024, and recognising the input is not critical is consistent with the ordering and carry-over causes.
errors.name: Second derivative test applied where the first derivative is not zero
non_conceptual_causes: the critical points are not computed before the test is applied
the input is taken from the stem's list of times rather than from the derivative's zeros
the second derivative is used because it is what the previous part produced
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the second derivative at an input that is not a critical point and classifies it.
errors.scoring_consequence: The conclusion does not follow and the justification point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask the student to sketch a curve concave down at a critical point: naming that shape a minimum is consistent with BC-MIS-05023, classifying from the derivative's value rather than its change is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, and a correct sketch beside the opposite written answer is consistent with the recall and sign causes.
errors.name: Sign convention of the second derivative test reversed
non_conceptual_causes: the two cases of the rule are recalled transposed
a sign is dropped while evaluating the second derivative
the answer sentence is written from the wrong row of a memorised table
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports a relative minimum where the second derivative is negative, or the reverse.
errors.scoring_consequence: The classification is wrong and the point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the first derivative does on each side of the input: reading the zero as a verdict is consistent with BC-MIS-05023, expecting either test to serve here is consistent with BC-MIS-05024, and running the first derivative test correctly once prompted is consistent with the shortcut and timing causes.
errors.name: Inconclusive case treated as a conclusion
non_conceptual_causes: the value zero is read as the test's third outcome
the first derivative chart is not drawn because the second derivative was quicker
the part ends before the fallback test is attempted
errors.observed_behavior: The response reports neither a maximum nor a minimum because the second derivative is zero at the critical point.
errors.scoring_consequence: The classification is unsupported, since the test settles nothing in that case.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many critical points the function has on the interval: an answer that a local test settles the global question is consistent with BC-MIS-05018, an answer that a relative extremum is automatically absolute is consistent with BC-MIS-05007, and supplying the uniqueness sentence on request is consistent with the transfer and timing causes.
errors.name: Sole critical point claim made without stating uniqueness
non_conceptual_causes: the uniqueness sentence is held in mind and never written
the interval is not scanned for further zeros of the derivative
the justification is written last and cut back to the classification alone
errors.observed_behavior: The response extends a relative extremum to an absolute one without saying that there is only one critical point on the interval.
errors.scoring_consequence: The justification is incomplete because the step that makes the local claim global is missing.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which derivative the supplied object actually shows: an answer that either test works anywhere is consistent with BC-MIS-05024, an answer that the plotted curve is the function is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, and identifying the object correctly while still choosing that test is consistent with the habit and assumption causes.
errors.name: Derivative test chosen that the given information cannot support
non_conceptual_causes: the figure is read as the graph of the function
the test used in the previous part is reused out of habit
the second derivative is assumed available because the stem mentions concavity
errors.observed_behavior: The response reaches for a second derivative test when only a graph of the first derivative is given and its slope is never discussed.
errors.scoring_consequence: The argument cannot be completed from the given information, so the justification point is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where the original curve has a horizontal tangent: an answer that places it at the curve's zeros is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, an answer that conflates bending with direction is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, and marking the horizontal tangents correctly on request is consistent with the shared axes and figure marking causes.
errors.name: Derivative sketch drawn with turning points at the zeros of the function
non_conceptual_causes: both curves are sketched on the same axes and features are transferred across
the zeros are the only marked features on the supplied figure
the sketch is drawn from the shape of a remembered example
errors.observed_behavior: The response places the extrema of the derivative sketch where the original curve crosses the axis.
errors.scoring_consequence: The sketch fails every feature check that follows.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the derivative is at a point where the function has a relative maximum: an answer drawn from the plotted curve's own turning points is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, an answer that the derivative fixes the function outright is consistent with BC-MIS-05025, and answering zero at once is consistent with the transposition and copying causes.
errors.name: Curve sketched with turning points at the zeros of the wrong object
non_conceptual_causes: the roles of the two plotted objects are transposed at the start of the sketch
the figure's caption is not read
the sketch is copied from an earlier part with the axes relabelled
errors.observed_behavior: The response draws the function with extrema where the derivative graph turns rather than where it crosses the axis.
errors.scoring_consequence: Extrema and points of inflection are interchanged throughout the sketch.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which derivative must change sign for an extremum and which for a point of inflection: taking the plotted curve for the function is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, conflating concavity with monotonicity is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, and stating the rule correctly beside the swapped table is consistent with the transposition and transcription causes.
errors.name: Feature of the function matched with the wrong derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the two derivative orders are transposed in the answer table
the matching is done from the shapes alone with no test point
the labels are correct on scratch work and swapped in transcription
errors.observed_behavior: The response pairs a point of inflection with a zero of the first derivative, or an extremum with a zero of the second.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every answer that rests on the correspondence is displaced by one derivative.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask where the derivative graph reaches its own extreme value: placing the bend at a horizontal tangent is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, treating any marked input as an inflection point is consistent with BC-MIS-05021, and locating it correctly on request is consistent with the freehand and figure marking causes.
errors.name: Point of inflection drawn at a turning point of the sketch
non_conceptual_causes: the sketch is drawn freehand and the bend lands at the marked point
the only marked inputs on the figure are the turning points
the second derivative information is not used because it was not asked for by name
errors.observed_behavior: The sketch puts a change of bending exactly where the curve has a horizontal tangent with no justification.
errors.scoring_consequence: The sketch contradicts the derivative information it was built from.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether shifting the sketch up by one unit would still fit the derivative: an answer of no is consistent with BC-MIS-05025, an answer that the plotted curve was the function all along is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, and an answer of yes with the uniqueness claim still written is consistent with the constant and article causes.
errors.name: Sketch treated as unique with no reference to the constant
non_conceptual_causes: the constant of integration is dropped in the antiderivative
no initial condition is supplied and one is read off the figure
the article in the phrase a graph of the function is skimmed
errors.observed_behavior: The response asserts that one particular curve is the graph of the function when only the derivative was supplied.
errors.scoring_consequence: The claim is stronger than the information supports unless a value of the function was given.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which curve has zeros at the turning points of which other curve: an ordering argued from appearance is consistent with BC-MIS-05011, an ordering that mixes bending with direction is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, and a correct ordering once the turning points are used is consistent with the key order and single test causes.
errors.name: Three graphs ordered in the reverse derivative direction
non_conceptual_causes: the curves are labelled in the order they appear in the figure's key
the ordering is tested at one input only
the labels are assigned from the amplitudes rather than from the turning points
errors.observed_behavior: The response labels the function as the second derivative and the second derivative as the function.
errors.scoring_consequence: Every feature question about the triple is answered about the wrong object.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the sign, not the direction, of the second derivative on that stretch: an answer given as rising or falling is consistent with BC-MIS-05020, an answer that the second derivative behaves like the first is consistent with BC-MIS-05019, and a correct sign with the written word wrong is consistent with the carry-over and wording causes.
errors.name: Concavity read from the wrong direction of the second derivative
non_conceptual_causes: the word decreasing is carried over from the previous part's question
the sign chart is built from the slopes of the second derivative
the words rising and positive are used interchangeably in the answer sentence
errors.observed_behavior: The response states that the graph is concave up where the second derivative is decreasing rather than positive.
errors.scoring_consequence: The concavity claim is wrong and any inflection list built from it inherits the error.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which expression has to change sign for the behaviour in question: an answer naming the function is consistent with BC-MIS-05010, an answer that ignores the domain partition points is consistent with BC-MIS-05012, and naming the derivative correctly beside the wrong chart is consistent with the carry-over and copying causes.
errors.name: Sign table built on the zeros of the function
non_conceptual_causes: the function's zeros are the values already solved for in an earlier part
the factored function is used where the factored derivative was needed
the chart is copied from the previous part with new labels
errors.observed_behavior: The response partitions the number line at the zeros of the function instead of at the zeros of its derivatives.
errors.scoring_consequence: The partition does not align with the sign changes that matter, so the reported behaviour is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether another function through the same table could behave differently between the listed inputs: an answer of no is consistent with BC-MIS-05026, an answer that fixes on the last tabulated value is consistent with BC-MIS-05017, and an answer of yes with the claim still written is consistent with the interpolation and answering causes.
errors.name: Finite table read as settling behaviour between the listed inputs
non_conceptual_causes: the tabulated values are joined by an assumed straight line
the word interval in the stem is read as the listed inputs
the claim is written because the table is the only evidence supplied and the part must be answered
errors.observed_behavior: The response claims monotonicity or concavity across a whole interval from three tabulated derivative values.
errors.scoring_consequence: The claim exceeds what the data support and cannot earn a justification point.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what each letter stands for and in what units: an answer that the first expression on the page is the objective is consistent with BC-MIS-05027, an answer that the variable ranges over all inputs is consistent with BC-MIS-05028, and fluent definitions with the sentence missing on paper is consistent with the template and transfer causes.
errors.name: Variables used without being defined
non_conceptual_causes: the letters are taken from a memorised template for this shape
the definitions are written on the diagram and not in the response
the setup is done quickly and the naming sentence is skipped
errors.observed_behavior: The response writes an objective and a constraint in letters that are never given meanings or units.
errors.scoring_consequence: The setup point is at risk and the interpretation that follows has nothing to name.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how many unknowns remain in the expression about to be differentiated: an answer that the first expression is already the objective is consistent with BC-MIS-05027, an answer that a critical point finishes the problem is consistent with BC-MIS-05029, and counting two unknowns at once is consistent with the abandoned substitution and misread task causes.
errors.name: Constraint not substituted, leaving two variables
non_conceptual_causes: the constraint is written down and never used
the substitution is begun and abandoned because the algebra is heavy
the two expressions are differentiated separately in the belief that both are wanted
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates an expression that still contains both unknowns.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is not the derivative of a one variable objective, so the critical point is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which values of the variable the situation permits: an answer of all inputs is consistent with BC-MIS-05028, an answer that only the critical points matter is consistent with BC-MIS-05016, and naming the physical limits at once is consistent with the assembly and transfer causes.
errors.name: Contextual domain omitted or taken as all inputs
non_conceptual_causes: the physical limits are stated in words in the stem and never assembled into an interval
the domain sentence is written on scratch work
the setup is copied from a formula sheet and answered as a bare exercise
errors.observed_behavior: The response never states the range of inputs the situation allows and treats the objective as defined everywhere.
errors.scoring_consequence: Endpoints that could hold the extremum are never considered and the verification is incomplete.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which variable the reduced objective is a function of: an answer naming whatever appears first is consistent with BC-MIS-05027, an answer that treats the eliminated variable as a constant is consistent with BC-MIS-05033, and naming it correctly beside the wrong differentiation is consistent with the ordering and transposition causes.
errors.name: Objective differentiated with respect to the wrong variable
non_conceptual_causes: the letter differentiated against is the one appearing first in the expression
the substitution is performed after the differentiation out of habit
the variable names are transposed when the reduced objective is copied
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates with respect to a variable that the constraint has already eliminated.
errors.scoring_consequence: The derivative is meaningless for the reduced objective and the critical point is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask how the student knows the critical point is not the opposite kind of extremum: an answer that finding it was enough is consistent with BC-MIS-05029, an answer that a local test settles the global question is consistent with BC-MIS-05018, and producing the sign argument on request is consistent with the timing and transfer causes.
errors.name: No verification that the critical point gives the extremum
non_conceptual_causes: the verification sentence is left to the end of the part and not reached
the sign chart is drawn on scratch work and not transferred
the answer is judged obvious from the shape of the objective
errors.observed_behavior: The response stops once the derivative is zero and reports the value as the maximum or minimum.
errors.scoring_consequence: The verification point is lost, and the reported extremum is unsupported on the stated domain.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what the number counts or measures: an answer that the value and its meaning are separate concerns is consistent with BC-MIS-07023, an answer that units are decoration is consistent with BC-MIS-04003, and naming the units at once is consistent with the transfer and timing causes.
errors.name: Units omitted from the reported optimum
non_conceptual_causes: the units are written in the setup and not repeated on the answer line
the objective and the constraint carry different units and neither is chosen
the part is finished at the end of the question with the answer line filled last
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives a number for the optimal value and never names its units.
errors.scoring_consequence: An interpretation point that requires units is lost.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask what would change in the sentence if the interval were different: an answer that nothing would change is consistent with BC-MIS-07023, an answer that conflates the extremum's location with its value is consistent with BC-MIS-05015, and a complete sentence on request is consistent with the copying and timing causes.
errors.name: Interpretation omits the quantity or the input where the extremum occurs
non_conceptual_causes: the sentence is copied from the previous part with the number changed
the interval is not named because it already appears in the stem
the interpretation is written last in the shortest form to hand
errors.observed_behavior: The interpretation sentence names a number without saying what it measures or when it is attained.
errors.scoring_consequence: The interpretation point is lost because the sentence is incomplete.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the value of the denominator at the reported point: an answer that only the numerator matters is consistent with BC-MIS-05031, an answer that one coordinate names the point is consistent with BC-MIS-05032, and discarding the point once the denominator is evaluated is consistent with the cancellation and solver causes.
errors.name: Horizontal tangent points found without checking the denominator
non_conceptual_causes: the denominator is cancelled before the numerator is set to zero
the derivative expression is copied without its denominator
every root the solver returns for the numerator is reported
errors.observed_behavior: The response sets the numerator of the derivative to zero and reports points where the denominator also vanishes.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported points may have no tangent at all, so the critical point list is wrong.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask whether the reported coordinates satisfy the defining equation: an answer that one coordinate is enough is consistent with BC-MIS-05032, an answer that the derivative alone settles the tangency is consistent with BC-MIS-05031, and substituting back on request is consistent with the revisiting and solver causes.
errors.name: Vertical tangent points reported without a matching point on the relation
non_conceptual_causes: the defining equation is not revisited after the denominator is solved
one coordinate is solved for and the other is assumed free
the solutions are reported in the single variable form the solver returned
errors.observed_behavior: The response solves the denominator equal to zero and reports the solutions without checking they lie on the curve.
errors.scoring_consequence: The reported points are not on the relation, so the answer is unsupported.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which points of the curve have that input value: an answer that one number names the point is consistent with BC-MIS-05032, an answer that conflates a location with a value is consistent with BC-MIS-05015, and supplying both coordinates on request is consistent with the timing and transfer causes.
errors.name: One coordinate reported where a point was asked for
non_conceptual_causes: the second coordinate needs the relation solved again and the part ends first
the word point in the stem is skimmed
the pair is written on scratch work and one number is transferred
errors.observed_behavior: The response gives an input value alone as the location of a horizontal tangent on a relation.
errors.scoring_consequence: The answer is incomplete because a relation may pass through several outputs at that input.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask for the derivative of the square of the dependent variable with respect to the independent one: an answer without the chain rule factor is consistent with BC-MIS-05033, an answer that the relation determines one function outright is consistent with BC-MIS-05025, and the correct factor supplied on request is consistent with the transcription and substitution causes.
errors.name: Second derivative of a relation taken as though the second variable were constant
non_conceptual_causes: the dependent variable is treated as constant because it carries no visible prime
the chain rule factor is written on scratch work and dropped in the copy
the quotient rule is applied and the inner derivative is never substituted back
errors.observed_behavior: The response differentiates the derivative expression without applying the chain rule to the dependent variable.
errors.scoring_consequence: The differentiation point is lost, and the value point remains available only through a correct substitution.

errors.discriminating_probe: Ask which way the curve bends when the second derivative is negative: a transposed answer is consistent with BC-MIS-05023, a classification drawn from the derivative's size is consistent with BC-MIS-05014, and a correct bending answer beside the opposite written classification is consistent with the sign and transposition causes.
errors.name: Sign of the second derivative at the point misread for the classification
non_conceptual_causes: a sign is dropped while substituting the point into the second derivative
the classification words are transposed in the answer sentence
the first derivative value is not set to zero before the evaluation
errors.observed_behavior: The response evaluates the second derivative on a relation correctly but classifies the point the wrong way round.
errors.scoring_consequence: The classification is wrong although the computation was right.
